principles.statement: When a loop or fan-out seems slow or large, add real captured metrics (counts, durations, distributions) and wait for completion — never bound it first and hope.
principles.rationale: Live 2026-09-20: a linking fan-out was capped at 8 candidates on a guess; the cap was wrong twice over — the real cause of the slowness was a deadlock, and after the fix the uncapped path ran 80x faster than the capped guess assumed it needed.

principles.statement: Every optimization claim must carry a before/after pair from the same instrumented surface.
principles.rationale: The keep-alive client change was accepted on the strength of 13,106ms -> 199ms on identical work (~80x per edge) — numbers from link_metrics, not intuition.

principles.statement: Caps hide the disease they were prescribed for: once a limit exists, the symptom stops being observable.
principles.rationale: A bounded fan-out cannot tell you its natural size; the uncapped run is the only instrument that measures the real workload.

heuristics.name: Observing latency or cardinality that looks wrong in any loop, fan-out, or search.
heuristics.description: Instrument first: counts in/out, failures, duration, and the largest observed item. Change nothing until one full real workload completes uncapped.

heuristics.name: Someone proposes a LIMIT as a fix.
heuristics.description: Require the measured numbers that justify the specific limit value, and a stated plan for removing it once the real cause is fixed.

decision_rules.condition: A slow path invites a cap, batch, or early-exit 'while we're here'.
decision_rules.action: Refuse until the instrumented numbers exist; then optimize the measured dominant cost (it is usually not the one the slowness suggested).
